key_insight: DemoPSD shows that self-distillation for reasoning LLMs can be improved by modulating teacher guidance based on disagreement, reducing overfitting to privileged token-level supervision and encouraging better exploration. The result is a more robust policy update that generalizes better across domains.
problem_solved: The paper addresses a key weakness of on-policy self-distillation: dense teacher supervision can make the student overfit to in-domain patterns, suppress exploration, and reduce cross-domain generalization when the teacher has access to privileged information.
method: Uses disagreement between teacher and student signals to adapt how strongly the teacher supervises the student.
Limits or softens token-level guidance when teacher predictions appear overly confident or misaligned, reducing harmful imitation.
Trains the model in an on-policy self-distillation setup so the same LLM can act as both teacher and student with different information access.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this suggests a practical way to train reasoning models that are less brittle and more transferable beyond the training domain. It can improve robustness without abandoning the efficiency benefits of self-distillation.
